original_question: For integer polygons, each angle has an LLS-sequence, and the LLS-sequence is the complete invariant of an integer angle in this setting. Classify all n-tuples of LLS-sequences that can occur as the angle data of integer n-gons.
correct_elements: The draft is very close to the paper's actual target. It correctly identifies that the relevant invariant attached to each integer angle is its LLS-sequence, that this invariant is complete for integer angles, and that the problem is to classify which n-tuples of such angle invariants can be realized by integer n-gons.
missing_details: The ambient setting should be made explicit: the problem is two-dimensional, in the plane with the standard integer lattice Z^2.
An integer n-gon should be defined as a polygon all of whose vertices are integer points.
The problem is for a fixed integer n (implicitly n >= 3), not for all n simultaneously in one statement.
The tuple is an ordered angle datum: it is the n-tuple of the polygon's angles taken in boundary order, not just an unordered collection of sequences.
The phrase 'LLS-sequence' should be tied to the paper's meaning from Section 1.2: it is the complete invariant of an integer angle up to affine lattice-preserving transformations.
The paper also records an equivalent toric-surface formulation, which is part of the official context and is absent from the draft.
The status note in the paper is relevant context: partial answers are known, including a complete answer for triangles, while the full classification is still unknown for n >= 4.
refined_question: For a fixed integer n >= 3, determine exactly which ordered n-tuples (S_1,...,S_n) of LLS-sequences can occur as the successive angle data of an integer n-gon in the plane R^2 with vertices in Z^2, where each vertex angle is regarded as an integer angle and encoded by its LLS-sequence, the complete invariant of integer angles up to affine lattice-preserving transformations.
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, classify toric surfaces with prescribed singularities among toric surfaces with a given Euler characteristic.
justification: The draft is essentially a near-verbatim restatement of Problem 2 in Section 1.3. I only sharpened it by making explicit the ambient lattice plane, the meaning of 'integer n-gon', the fact that n is fixed, and that the data form an ordered angle tuple around the polygon. I did not broaden the question to convex polygons, higher dimensions, or other variants, because the paper's stated target is exactly this two-dimensional angle-classification problem. The alternate toric-surface version is included because the paper explicitly states that equivalence right after Problem 2. The surrounding text in Sections 1.1 and 1.2 is exactly the context needed to make the question stand alone: it defines integer polygons and explains why LLS-sequences are the correct complete invariants for integer angles.

citations.label: Discussion of LLS-sequences; statement that the LLS-sequence is the complete invariant of integer angles
Remark after Problem 2: equivalence with a toric-surface classification problem; triangles solved; full description unknown for n >= 4
